recovered.name: Entity came back
recovered.description: Fires when an entity comes back after having been unavailable for a while, so a router rebooting does not read as everything in the house recovering.

for.name: For
for.description: How long the entity has to have been away before coming back counts. Anything shorter is a flicker: reloading an integration takes every one of its entities through unavailable and back inside a second.

sequence.name: Triggers in order
sequence.description: Fires when several triggers happen one after another, in the order given.

steps.name: Steps
steps.description: The triggers that have to happen, in order. Only the one being waited for is listening, so a later step firing early is not a match.

timeout.name: Timeout
timeout.description: How long the whole sequence may take, counted from the first step. Left out, it waits indefinitely.

reset.name: Reset
reset.description: Triggers that abandon a sequence already under way, putting it back to waiting for the first step.

while.name: While a condition holds
while.description: Fires when a condition turns true, and keeps firing on an interval for as long as it stays true.

condition.name: Condition
condition.description: The condition to watch. Firing starts when it turns true and stops when it stops being true.

every.name: Every
every.description: How long to wait between one firing and the next, for as long as the condition holds.

watchdog.name: Watchdog
watchdog.description: Fires when something that was expected to happen does not happen in time.

arm.name: Arm
arm.description: What starts the watch. The wait is measured from here, and arming again while already waiting starts the wait over.

expect.name: Expect
expect.description: What is expected to follow. Arriving in time calls the watch off, and nothing fires.

within.name: Within
within.description: How long the expected thing has to arrive. This fires when that time passes and it has not.

flapping.name: Entity will not settle
flapping.description: Fires when an entity changes state more often than it should within a stretch of time.

changes.name: Changes
changes.description: How many changes of state it takes before this fires. Changes of attribute do not count, and neither does an entity appearing or disappearing.

within.name: Within
within.description: The stretch of time those changes have to fall inside. It slides along, so this is always about the most recent changes.

condition_met.name: Condition turned true
condition_met.description: Fires when a condition goes from false to true, using the same condition building blocks as anywhere else.

cron.name: Cron schedule
cron.description: Fires on a crontab schedule, for the times Home Assistant's own time triggers cannot express, like every weekday at seven or the last Friday of the month.

schedule.name: Schedule
schedule.description: A crontab expression with five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. Supports ranges and steps, and the day-of-week extensions, so "MON#2" is the second Monday and "5L" the last Friday. Nicknames like "@daily" are not supported.

integration_failed.name: Integration failed to set up
integration_failed.description: Fires when a configuration entry has been unable to set itself up for a while, past the point where Home Assistant's own retries would have sorted it out.

for.name: For
for.description: How long an entry has to keep failing before this fires. Home Assistant retries a failing entry every ten minutes at the slowest, so anything shorter than that reports trouble that may still fix itself.

entry_id.name: Entries
entry_id.description: Limit this to particular configuration entries. Leave it empty to watch every one of them.

repair_issue_created.name: Repair issue created
repair_issue_created.description: Fires when a new repair issue turns up, so you can hear about one without visiting the repairs page.

domain.name: Integrations
domain.description: Limit this to issues reported by particular integrations, by their domain. Leave it empty for all of them.

severity.name: Severity
severity.description: Limit this to issues of a particular severity. Leave it empty for all of them.

repair_issue_removed.name: Repair issue resolved
repair_issue_removed.description: Fires when a repair issue goes away, either fixed or no longer reported.

domain.name: Integrations
domain.description: Limit this to issues reported by particular integrations, by their domain. Leave it empty for all of them.

stale.name: Entity fell silent
stale.description: Fires when nothing has written to an entity for a while, which catches a device that died quietly rather than going unavailable.

for.name: For
for.description: How long an entity has to stay silent before this fires. An entity that keeps reporting the same value is not silent.

repair_issue_present.name: Repair issue outstanding
repair_issue_present.description: Passes while a repair issue is outstanding. Issues somebody has ignored do not count.

domain.name: Integrations
domain.description: Limit this to issues reported by particular integrations, by their domain. Leave it empty for all of them.

severity.name: Severity
severity.description: Limit this to issues of a particular severity. Leave it empty for all of them.

quota.name: Run allowance left
quota.description: Passes while this automation has run fewer than a given number of times within a given period. Scripts are not counted.

limit.name: Limit
limit.description: How many runs are allowed within the period.

period.name: Period
period.description: The window the limit applies to. It rolls, so a day means any twenty-four hours rather than between midnights.

triggered_by_automation.name: Triggered by an automation
triggered_by_automation.description: Passes when another automation set this run going, whether it did so directly or through a script.

automation.name: Automations
automation.description: Limit this to particular automations. Leave it empty to accept any of them.

triggered_by_user.name: Triggered by a user
triggered_by_user.description: Passes when a person is behind what set this off: a state change or an event they caused, including one that made a template trigger become true. A schedule, the sun, or an integration acting on its own carries nobody, and neither does forcing a run with the Run button.

person.name: People
person.description: Only pass when one of these people started it. Leave empty to pass for anyone. A person has to have a user account linked to them, otherwise there is nothing to match against.

not_triggered_by_user.name: Not triggered by a user
not_triggered_by_user.description: Passes when nobody can be held responsible for this run: a schedule, the sun, an integration acting on its own, or the Run button. Takes no options on purpose. To exclude specific people instead, put "Triggered by a user" inside a Not condition.

chance.name: Chance
chance.description: Passes a set percentage of the time, chosen at random each check. Handy for adding a bit of variation to your automations.

percentage.name: Percentage
percentage.description: How often this condition should pass, as a percentage.

cooldown.name: Cooldown
cooldown.description: Passes only if this automation or script has not run within the given time (or has never run). A built-in cooldown, so it does not re-fire too often.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: How long to wait after the last run before this condition passes again.

alert_unknown_entity_references.title: Unknown entity watched by alert: {alert}
alert_unknown_entity_references.description:
Spook has found a ghost in your alerts 👻

The alert {alert} (`{entity_id}`) watches an entity that is unknown to Home Assistant:

{entities}

An alert can only fire on the entity it watches, so this one can never fire again. It looks the same as an alert with nothing to report.

To fix this error, edit the `alert:` section in your configuration and point this alert at an entity that exists.

Spook 👻 Your homie.

alert_unknown_notifiers.title: Unknown notifiers used by alert: {alert}
alert_unknown_notifiers.description:
Spook has found a ghost in your alerts 👻

The alert {alert} (`{entity_id}`) notifies through the following actions, which are unknown to Home Assistant:

{notifiers}

The alert still fires and still does its rounds, but these notifications go nowhere. Home Assistant logs that only at the moment the alert fires, which is a poor moment to find out nobody is listening.

To fix this error, edit the `notifiers:` list of this alert in your configuration and remove or correct these entries.

Spook 👻 Your homie.

init.description:
Spook has found a ghost in your dashboards 👻

{resources}

Spook can clear the extra copies and keep the most recently added one.

Spook 👻 Your homie.

notify_unknown_group_members.description:
Spook has found a ghost in your notify groups 👻

The notify group `{group}` forwards to the following actions, which are unknown to Home Assistant:

{members}

The group still delivers to the rest of its members, and it still reports success to whatever called it, so nothing upstream notices. The failure surfaces only as a stray "Task exception was never retrieved" in the log, which names no group and reads like a bug. Whoever was behind that member simply stops being notified.

To fix this error, edit the `services:` list of this group in your configuration and remove or correct these entries.

Spook 👻 Your homie.
